summary: A 39-year-old male presents with acute, sharp left-sided chest pain starting approximately eight hours ago. The pain is described as 7-8/10 in severity, exacerbated by laying down and deep breathing, and associated with light-headedness, palpitations, and dyspnea. Family history is significant for a father with a history of myocardial infarction and cholesterol issues.
subjective.symptoms: sharp left-sided chest pain | light-headedness | shortness of breath | palpitations | neck swelling
assessment.differential_diagnosis: Myocardial infarction | Pericarditis | Musculoskeletal chest pain | Pulmonary embolism
plan.treatment_plan: Further diagnostic evaluation required given cardiac risk factors and symptom presentation.
